title: QUIC RFC 9000 Peer Connection-ID Lifecycle Runtime Verification
verification_method: Focused requirement-home execution, protected packet inspection for RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID emission, SpecTrace validation, and coverage-triage regeneration.
scope: This verification covers the bounded runtime peer connection-ID lifecycle seam: peer-issued connection-ID active set maintenance, increased Retire Prior To cleanup, protected RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID emission for retired lower sequences, local CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR handling for peer active-set excess, and local issuance rejection when an additional issued ID would exceed the peer limit.
expected_result: Focused tests prove positive, negative, and edge coverage for local and peer active connection-ID limit handling, peer-issued connection-ID set maintenance, and Retire Prior To retirement ordering. Nearby S19P15/S19P16 regression homes remain green so the existing frame-codec and RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID protocol-violation behavior is preserved.
procedure: Run the focused RFC 9000 peer connection-ID lifecycle requirement-home tests and nearby S19P15/S19P16 regression homes.
Confirm protected RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID emission by opening the protected application-data packet and scanning the payload frames.
Render and check touched SpecTrace artifacts.
Regenerate the QUIC requirement coverage triage.
preconditions: The runtime has a validated active path and 1-RTT packet protection material.
The peer NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame is received on the protected application-data path.
The local active_connection_id_limit defaults to the RFC 9000 minimum when the test bootstrap transport parameters do not explicitly set it.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This verification intentionally does not claim full S9P5 migration discipline, preferred-address transition behavior, new local route registration, public migration APIs, multipath behavior, or interop-runner migration success.

status_summary: Passed locally on 2026-05-03. The focused peer connection-ID lifecycle and nearby regression filter passed 17/17, proving the bounded peer CID active-set, Retire Prior To, and active-limit enforcement seam while keeping broader migration clusters out of scope.
